title: Throttled Retroflow Circuit for Usage Reprocessing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: Build a reusable orchestration pattern ("Retroflow Circuit") for tenant-scoped usage reprocessing that prioritizes cost predictability and graceful degradation. This ticket covers the design and initial implementation of the circuit: a coordinator service that computes minimal diff windows, enforces tenant-level throttles and budget caps, issues tokenized resume markers, and exposes per-run observability and safety gates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Circuit can accept a job spec and produce a sequence of windowed work units with resume tokens. 2) Each work unit enforces tenant-level max-ops-per-minute and budget caps. 3) System supports idempotent application of transforms (replay steps) with an idempotency marker. 4) End-to-end test demonstrating a multi-tenant run that throttles under cost stress and resumes from tokenized checkpoints without duplicates. 5) Dashboard widgets show run progress, projected cost, and failures per-tenant.
design_summary: The Retroflow Circuit is composed of three parts: (A) Planner: computes minimal coverage based on start/end timestamps, schema-change hints, and a heuristic 'diff-mosaic' that groups sparse updates into cost-efficient windows; (B) Executor: issues windowed tasks to the reprocessor with per-window budget allowances and tenant circuit-breaker logic; (C) Controller: coordinates resume tokens, backpressure signals, and safety checks (schema compatibility and snapshot validation). Planner will use an improved snapshot-compare engine that prefers read-amplification over compute-heavy diff when tenant data is small.
implementation_notes: - New service: retroflow-controller (go) behind internal API gateway. - Planner lives as a library packaged for both controller and a lightweight CLI for dry-runs. - Executor integrates with existing reprocessing worker queue (kafka topic: telemetry.reprocess.work). - Resume tokens are opaque base64 markers containing version, window_id, tenant_id, and checksum. - Budget caps persisted in tenant metadata (config service) and enforced by the controller before enqueue. - Idempotency: workers must check and set a per-window marker in the durable index (dynamo / cockroach) using compare-and-set semantics.
tasks: Design planner algorithm and diff-mosaic grouping (Aisha/Marco)
Prototype resume token format and serialization (Marco)
Add tenant budget enforcement hooks to controller (backend)
Integrate executor with telemetry.reprocess.work topic and add consumer group handling
End-to-end integration test with synthetic tenant workload (stress under cost cap)
Create Console dashboard panels: run progress, projected cost, tenant throttles
Security review: validate token encoding and ACLs
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Stronger throttling prevents cost overruns but lengthens backfill completion time. Tradeoff: provide 'emergency burst' option subject to manual approval.
- Resume tokens simplify resumes but leak task state; mitigating by encrypting tokens and scoping them to tenant.
- Grouping sparse diffs reduces overhead but increases chance of false positives requiring replays; mitigated by conservative grouping thresholds and dry-run simulation mode.
monitoring_and_metrics: Expose metrics: windows_queued, windows_processed, windows_failed, avg_window_runtime_ms, tenant_cost_incurred, tenant_throttle_rate, resume_token_restarts. Add traces for planner decisions and include planner_reason tag (e.g., SCHEMA_HINT, SIZE_THRESHOLD, DENSITY_BUCKET).
dashboards_and_alerts:
- Console: Retroflow -> Active runs table, per-tenant cost burn rate gauge.
- Alert: tenant_throttle_rate > 0.5 for > 10m -> pager (P1).
- Alert: avg_window_runtime_ms > 3x expected -> SRE channel.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag controller behind internal toggle. 2) Run dry-runs on staging with 3 synthetic tenants and compare with baseline. 3) Enable for low-risk tenant cohort (alpha) with strict budget caps. 4) Observe two weeks, adjust grouping thresholds, then expand to more tenants. 5) Offer opt-in emergency burst for 24h windows via Console with audit log.
notes: Follow-on tickets will add schema-migration-aware planners and a cost-prediction model to auto-tune window sizes. Consider integrating Optimize suggestions to recommend quantization/rewrite policies for heavy tenants to reduce reprocess cost.
